sections.title: Letter ípsilon sound
paragraphs: The letter name is (ípsilon) /ˈipsilõ/. Its main sound is heard in the word (yoga) /ˈjɔ.ɡɐ/, a form of exercise. This letter makes two sounds.

sections.title: How to say ípsilon
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the middle of your tongue high toward the roof of your mouth. Keep your lips wide. For the second sound, keep your lips wide and your tongue high in front. Both sounds are voiced. A voiced sound makes your vocal cords shake. Touch your throat to feel the buzz.

sections.title: Spelling of ípsilon
paragraphs: This letter works as a semivowel when it sits next to a vowel. A semivowel is a short sound that acts like a consonant, as in (yoga) /ˈjɔ.ɡɐ/ or (playboy) /plɐjˈbɔj/. It works as a full vowel in borrowed words and names. You hear this vowel in (nylon) /ˈnaj.lõ/ and (Sydney) /ˈsid.nej/.

sections.title: Comparing ípsilon sounds
paragraphs: Do not turn this letter into a harsh friction sound like the start of yellow. Keep the airflow smooth and open. When it is a vowel, do not make it long or broad like the sound in see. Keep the sound short and clean.
